# Operator prompt evidence

Our metropolitan heat-response office needs one workspace for deciding whether a proposed heat-response activation window is operationally ready. A forecast alone is not enough: we can open a cooling route only when the route, cooling locations and supporting city services are usable. The product will assemble the readiness evidence for a duty controller. It must not send public alerts, dispatch crews or control utilities.

The durable work item is a heat-response window record, containing the geographic coverage, start and end time, source snapshots, interpretation, route constraints and activation-readiness decision. Its lifecycle is collecting, assessed, ready and closed; a blocked window stays assessed with its reasons. Source exports and cooling-site references are attachments and fields of this record, not separately governed workflows. A closed record means the office has verified its readiness decision and evidence, not that a live emergency operation has been dispatched.

The heat coordinator opens the record with its coverage and time window. The meteorologist associates the forecast and observations and records the heat interpretation. The public-health lead records the vulnerability and exposure assessment using the permitted aggregate evidence. The access planner records whether the proposed cooling routes and sites can be used with the available service conditions. The duty controller records the activation-readiness decision after checking the evidence and blocking conditions. The heat coordinator verifies that the decision names the same window and source revisions, then closes the record. Those are the human responsibilities for the first complete path.

The implementation should have a window desk owning the record and lifecycle, a source snapshot binder retaining the supplied exports and their provenance, an assessment workspace recording the meteorologist's, public-health lead's and access planner's evidence, and a readiness gate checking prerequisites and retaining the controller's decision. The binder is not a live integration hub. Staff attach approved exports from the independently operated services below. The assessment workspace keeps their different meanings visible instead of flattening every value into a generic severity number.

The regional weather forecast service is operated by the forecasting office and is authoritative for forecast issue time and its stated uncertainty. The urban mesonet service is operated by the city's sensor unit and is authoritative for observed air temperature at street stations. The satellite thermal archive is operated by the remote-sensing laboratory and is authoritative for the acquisition time and footprint of surface-temperature imagery. The regional air-quality service is operated by the clean-air district and is authoritative for its monitored pollution advisories. The smoke-dispersion service is operated by the wildfire coordination office and is authoritative for modeled smoke arrival windows.

The electricity outage bulletin service belongs to the distribution utility and identifies unavailable supply areas. The drinking-water pressure service belongs to the water utility and identifies low-pressure zones affecting drinking-water access. The transit service-alert system belongs to the transit operator and identifies suspended accessible routes. The street-closure register belongs to the roads department and identifies temporary pedestrian barriers. The cooling-building capacity system belongs to the municipal property team and identifies available occupied capacity and opening hours. The elevator availability system belongs to the contracted building-maintenance operator and identifies lifts that cannot serve a cooling location.

The emergency medical demand summary belongs to ambulance control and contains only aggregate call pressure. The heat-illness surveillance system belongs to public health and contains delayed aggregate presentations, not a live patient list. The outreach coverage register belongs to social services and identifies neighborhoods with an available outreach team, without naming residents. The accessible-vehicle availability service belongs to the contracted mobility operator and identifies aggregate vehicle capacity for the proposed window. The public drinking-fountain inspection register belongs to parks operations and identifies fountains currently closed after inspection. The overnight shelter availability service belongs to the regional housing partnership and identifies approved overnight capacity when a heat window crosses midnight.

All of these source relationships are part of the requested product. Each has its own operator, collection or operational authority and snapshot time. They do not become additional human steps merely because the record depends on their evidence. In particular, retain the elevator service and drinking-fountain register even when their exports say no problem was found. An unavailable export is an explicit missing input; it is never a reassuring zero. The product receives no account credentials and has no authority to fetch private data or change an upstream system.

Do not represent modeled surface heat or smoke as observed air temperature. Preserve forecast issue time separately from observation time. A source export outside the requested window must be marked inapplicable rather than silently reused. No resident or patient identity may enter the record. The duty controller alone records the activation-readiness decision. A cooling location with no usable accessible route cannot support a ready decision. A location without supply for its required cooling equipment cannot contribute its advertised capacity. Duplicate contributions from building and shelter exports for the same location cannot increase available capacity. Missing lift status blocks reliance on a lift-dependent route. Changing a source snapshot after the controller's decision invalidates that decision until it is reviewed again. Retain the earlier decision and its source revisions when it is invalidated. The system must never dispatch crews or send a public heat alert.

The finished record must make the forecast, observation, exposure, service availability, accessible-route evidence, blocking conditions and attributable readiness decision inspectable for the same window. We want ordinary staff upload and review screens; source procurement, public communications and operational dispatch remain with their existing owners.

The access planner must attach an acknowledgement from the housing partnership that the overnight capacity cited for that window is still available at the handoff time. The duty controller must check that acknowledgement before recording readiness for an overnight window. The readiness gate must leave such a window assessed if the acknowledgement is missing or names another night. Retain the original shelter snapshot, every other source relationship and all previous assessment evidence on the same heat-response window record; the acknowledgement supplements them rather than replacing them.

# Operator prompt evidence

We are opening a hospital site for a sponsor-led clinical trial and need a workspace that assembles the site's readiness handoffs before the site is marked open in our operations register. It is an evidence and coordination product, not an ethics board or a clinical decision maker. Every specialist below is accountable for a different handoff in our existing process; none can sign for another simply because both work for the hospital.

Use one trial site activation dossier for the site and trial reference. It carries the required references, scope statements, signed checks and final readiness decision. Its states are assembling, held, ready for chair review and open for operations. A held dossier retains its completed handoffs. Trial participants, medicines, specimens, staff and study data are referenced context, not new governed objects managed by this product. The first release ends with the readiness chair's attributable decision and the resulting recorded operational status. It does not enroll a participant.

The trial coordinator opens the dossier with the trial-registry identifier and hospital site. The site principal investigator records the proposed operational scope and permitted participant population. The sponsor representative records the sponsor's site authorization reference. The ethics liaison attaches the actual reviewing committee's decision reference and validity period. The consent specialist attaches the version of the consent materials that matches that decision. The language-access reviewer records which consent translations are supported at the site. The accessibility reviewer records the visit and materials accommodation arrangements.

The trial pharmacist records the investigational-supply handling signoff. The laboratory director records the local assay-capacity signoff. The specimen logistics officer records the specimen handoff and transport arrangement. The data manager records the mapping between the site's collection forms and the sponsor's dataset specification. The statistician records the match between the supplied randomization specification and the trial version. The privacy officer records the approved site-to-sponsor data-flow terms. The security reviewer records the access-control readiness check for the collection workspace. The site operations lead records the staffing coverage for the agreed visit schedule. The training coordinator records the study-specific staff training evidence. The readiness chair records the site's operational readiness decision on the completed handoffs. This is the first complete trip through the dossier; the specialist steps are handoffs, not independent products.

The software should have an activation desk owning the dossier and lifecycle, an evidence registry retaining the versioned references and attachments, a handoff gate checking completeness and authority, and an operations-status journal retaining the chair's decision and subsequent invalidations. It may check that the declared inputs are present and current; it cannot make the specialist's professional decision. The journal records operational readiness only after the chair's approval.

The sponsor's trial registry is the source of the trial version and site authorization references. The reviewing committee's document portal is the source of the ethics decision; it remains an explicitly linked authority even though it takes no action in our first path. The hospital's learning system is the source of the training completion export. The clinical laboratory's capacity register is the source of the assay availability reference, and the investigational pharmacy's handling register is the source of the supply-handling instruction revision. These are separately operated sources with different accountable custodians. Staff attach those references and exports using their existing access. This request grants no automatic login, trial-data access or authority to create a committee approval. Retain each source's identity and revision in the dossier.

Never describe an internal ready state as ethics approval. Do not admit patient identifiers or actual participant data into this workspace. Consent materials must remain tied to the decision and trial version they cover. An expired committee decision blocks an open-for-operations status. Missing study-specific training evidence blocks completion for staff assigned to the visit schedule. The collection-workspace access check must be recorded before readiness can be approved. Replacing a source decision or trial version invalidates affected handoffs and the prior operational decision without deleting them. Draft consent material and internal access-control evidence remain private to authorized site reviewers.

Success is an inspectable dossier showing the requested site and trial, every accountable handoff, the source revisions, the chair's decision and the verified operational status. Participant recruitment, treatment advice, sponsor database operation, investigational supply ordering and regulatory submissions remain outside this product.

Preserve the original sponsor authorization, committee reference, consent version and every specialist handoff on the same activation dossier. The final readiness evidence must retain the insurance confirmation with its source reference.

# Operator prompt evidence

Our river partnership is building a data handoff service for a cross-jurisdiction monitoring study. We need to assemble one agreed window of observations from separately operated collections, preserve their different authority and method claims, and prove that the study office acknowledged the exact packet we handed over. A uniform-looking table is not enough: laboratory results, operational readings and volunteer observations must remain distinguishable. The product must not turn this into a public publication service or silently retrieve data we have not been given.

The work item is a river federation transfer record for a catchment, time window and recipient study office. It carries source exports, access conditions, mapping decisions, limitations, review evidence, the packet digest and acknowledgement. Its states are collecting, reconciled, cleared for transfer, transferred and acknowledged. A rejected or incomplete packet stays in the same record with its earlier versions. We are not making a separate case for every observation or trying to replace the upstream data catalogs.

The federation coordinator opens the transfer record with its catchment, window and recipient. The source steward attaches the authorized exports and records their availability and conditions. The hydrologist records the reconciliation of measurement context and sampling coverage. The data quality reviewer records the disposition for the proposed transfer. The study liaison downloads the cleared packet and records the recipient's acknowledgement. The federation coordinator verifies that the acknowledgement names the submitted digest and marks the record acknowledged. That exact acknowledged transfer, with usable provenance, is the first complete result.

Use a transfer desk for the record and lifecycle, a provenance binder for source exports and conditions, a reconciliation workspace for mappings and limitations, and a packet-and-receipt workbench for the immutable transfer packet and digest match. The reconciliation workspace must preserve method and unit differences when the source evidence does not justify normalization. The workbench never treats file download as recipient acceptance.

The national park's headwater monitoring service is operated by the park science office and contains protected headwater sampling observations. The mountain hydrology office's snowmelt station service contains flow and snowmelt context for its upstream stations. The agricultural extension laboratory's runoff collection contains nutrient assays from its field-drain monitoring program. The city drinking-water laboratory's intake collection contains treated-supply intake test observations, with its own laboratory methods. The environmental regulator's discharge-monitoring exchange contains permitted industrial discharge returns and their reporting periods.

The mine-water inspectorate's seepage registry contains acidity and metal observations from licensed mine sites. The port authority's estuary sensor service contains salinity observations from its maintained harbor instruments. The tribal environmental office's watershed archive contains observations released under that office's stated sharing conditions; it is not interchangeable with the county's data. The university marine laboratory's coastal collection contains microbiology study observations and their research methods. The regional wastewater operator's effluent reporting service contains plant effluent measurements with its treatment-stage identifiers.

The municipal water utility's distribution-monitoring system contains residual measurements from the distribution network rather than the river itself. The public works department's stormwater event archive contains first-flush samples identified by storm event. The fisheries agency's spawning-stream service contains dissolved-oxygen observations for its habitat sites. The public recreation health unit's bathing-water collection contains bacteria samples used for its designated bathing locations. The transport authority's bridge-works monitoring portal contains sediment observations collected around active river works.

The reservoir operator's water-column service contains depth-specific profiles for its managed impoundment. The community science association's volunteer observation hub contains volunteer reports with the declared collection method and verification flag. Each of these collections has its own responsible operator, observation scope and export identity. All are required source relationships in the federation record, including when a collection supplies an explicit no-observations export for the agreed window. None is merely a background example. Staff attach the authorized snapshots; the product is not authorized to query those systems or acquire missing permissions.

Keep the original upstream collection and export identifiers with every transferred observation. Preserve observation time separately from export time. Never report an absent export as a collection with no observations. Do not mix water-column depths without retaining the supplied depth labels. Do not convert a laboratory result into a field-sensor observation. Preserve volunteer verification flags rather than promoting volunteer reports to certified assays. Enforce the tribal archive's supplied sharing restriction on the transfer packet. Do not include restricted sampling-location coordinates in an unauthorized recipient packet. Only the data quality reviewer may clear a packet for transfer. An altered source export after clearance invalidates the clearance before another packet can be produced. The recipient acknowledgement must match the exact packet digest. Retain a rejected packet and its rejection reason when a revised packet is prepared.

The evidence for completion is the catchment and window, the availability and authority of each collection, its access conditions, the preserved measurement context, the quality disposition, the exact packet and the matching acknowledgement. Legal adjudication of sharing rights, automatic upstream harvesting, operational pollution alarms and public publication are outside this request.

The study liaison must record the purpose stated in the recipient acknowledgement, and the source steward must confirm that this purpose is permitted by every attached collection's access conditions before the coordinator marks the record acknowledged. A matching digest alone is no longer sufficient. If a purpose is outside any collection's stated conditions, keep the record transferred with that restriction visible and retain the acknowledgement as evidence. Add this check to the existing packet-and-receipt workbench. Preserve all original collection relationships, mappings, limitations, clearance and packet versions on the same record.

# Operator prompt evidence

We need an evidence workspace for a ransomware recovery rehearsal of one business service in an isolated laboratory. Our continuity team currently has separate signoffs from specialists who control different parts of recovery. The product should let the recovery director see that one rehearsal restored the agreed test service and completed its safety checks. It must never run a recovery command or connect the laboratory to production.

Keep one isolated recovery rehearsal record for the agreed service and exercise window. The image references, custody trail, isolation checks, approved test data, backup reference, restoration evidence, timing observations and final decision belong to that record. Its lifecycle is preparing, isolated, restoring, verifying and complete. A stopped rehearsal stays in the record with its stop reason and preserved evidence. The software does not govern production incidents, backups or user identities as separate work items.

The rehearsal coordinator opens the record with the service and window. The forensic examiner records the agreed source-image digest and its examination limitations. The evidence custodian records the custody handoff for that image. The identity lead records that the test identities are separated from production identities. The network lead records the laboratory network-isolation check. The privacy officer records approval of the redacted test dataset. The backup operator records the immutable backup reference selected for the exercise. The storage lead attests that the restoration destination is the designated laboratory storage.

The cryptographic key custodian records the use of the approved exercise-key reference without revealing the key. The database operator records the database restoration validation. The endpoint lead records that the restored laboratory hosts have the required isolation configuration. The application owner records the application smoke-test result. The threat analyst records the check for the specified compromise indicators in the restored test service. The data integrity auditor records reconciliation of the agreed test ledger totals. The business process owner records the result of the agreed critical workflow exercise. The continuity manager records the measured recovery-time observations and their limitations. The recovery director records the rehearsal completion decision on the specialist evidence. Those handoffs are the first complete path, with distinct accountable roles; completing one does not authorize another specialist's decision.

The product should have a rehearsal desk for the work item and transitions, a custody-and-evidence vault for redacted attachments, a prerequisite gate for the isolation and authority checks, and a recovery proof journal for verification and the director's decision. The gate must be able to hold the rehearsal when a required specialist check is missing or negative. The journal must retain conflicting observations until the accountable specialist resolves them; it cannot invent a passing result.

The immutable backup catalog is the source of the selected backup reference. The laboratory service inventory is the source of the approved destination and sandbox identity. The exercise-key register is the source of the permitted key reference, the incident evidence archive is the source of the examiner's retained image digest, and the endpoint configuration register is the source of the approved laboratory-host isolation profile. Each source is operated under its own accountable custodian. They remain explicit source relationships even when their owners supply attachments manually and the systems perform no first-path action. The workspace gets no backup credentials, decryption keys, production directory connection or recovery automation permission.

No live credential or decryption key may be stored in the record. Test data must have the privacy officer's approval before it can be used in the rehearsal. A different backup or image digest invalidates later restoration and integrity evidence while preserving the earlier evidence. The recovery director cannot complete the rehearsal while any required specialist check is missing or negative. Measured recovery time must retain its actual start and end events and cannot be presented as a production recovery guarantee. A stopped rehearsal must retain its stop reason and all evidence already supplied. Only the recovery director may record the final completion decision.

We should finish with a complete record showing the exact image and backup, the isolation and test-data authority, specialist restoration and integrity checks, the critical workflow result, timing limitations and attributable completion decision. Live remediation, real incident containment, production failover, insurance claims and customer notification are outside this product.

Preserve the redacted restoration proof and its custody history in the evidence vault; cleanup must not delete the evidence needed to review the rehearsal. Keep every original specialist handoff and source relationship on the same isolated recovery rehearsal record.
